sections.changelog:
Added

  • **Field-length normalization.** A matching word in a long description now counts for less than the same word in a short title, so a full product whose specs merely mention a part no longer outranks the part itself. On by default; run a full reindex once so the length data it needs is available. Adjustable on the Relevance tab.
  • **"Searches saved" analytics.** The Analytics tab now shows how many searches were rescued from a dead end by the Russian-language recovery — a wrong keyboard layout swapped back, or a typo corrected — as visible proof of the value the plugin adds silently.
  • **Scheduled full rebuild (opt-in).** The index can now rebuild itself on a weekly or monthly schedule — a safety net for catalogs whose content is overwritten without updating its modified date, which the hourly catch-up relies on. Off by default; it runs in small background batches so a large catalog never rebuilds in one request. Set it on the Index tab.
  • **Index page-builder content (opt-in).** Text built with WPBakery, Divi or other shortcode-based builders can now be indexed and searched instead of being stripped out. Off by default because expanding shortcodes is heavier; it runs only during the background reindex. Enable on the Coverage tab and reindex.
  • **Aggressive typo correction (opt-in).** Typos can now be corrected on every query, not only when the results are already thin. A corrected phrase is adopted only when it finds more products, so a good result set is never replaced. Off by default; toggle on the General tab.
  • **Glued model codes are searchable by any part.** A run-together code like "gtx1660" now also matches "gtx" and "1660", and "4000mah" matches "4000" and "mah", so a shopper who types only part of a model still finds it. Ideal for electronics and spare parts; on by default, with a toggle on the Relevance tab to turn it off where size codes would be noise (apparel). Reindex to apply.
  • **Search-as-you-type in the dropdown.** The last, half-typed word is now matched as a prefix, so results appear before it is finished (e.g. "самс" already finds Samsung). Applies from three letters, ranks below exact matches, and is capped so a short prefix never slows the search. On by default; toggle on the General tab.
  • **Filter search results by category, brand and price.** A new "MVweb Search Filters" widget (and `[mvweb_ss_facets]` shortcode) shows the categories and brands the current query matches, each with a live count, plus a price range. Selecting them narrows the results and paginates the rest. Enabled by default; place the widget in a sidebar or the shortcode on the results page.
  • **`wp mvweb-ss eval-seed`** — builds a starter relevance test-set from the real search log (top queries + their current top results as a baseline), so ranking changes can be checked for regressions before they ship.
  • **Shoppers can sort search results.** A new `[mvweb_ss_sort]` shortcode adds a Relevance / Popularity / Rating / Price / Newest selector to the results page; relevance stays the default and the choice is carried in the URL.
  • **No-result inbox suggests a fix.** Each frequent "nothing found" query now shows its closest successful query, and the Synonym action pre-fills both as a ready pair — turning unmet searches into a one-click synonym. Uses only the existing aggregated log; no visitor tracking.
  • **Never a dead end on an empty search (WooCommerce).** When a query matches nothing, the live dropdown now offers best-selling products instead of a blank result, so the shopper keeps a way forward. On by default; toggle on the Relevance tab.
  • **"Did you mean…?" now shown by default.** When a typo or wrong keyboard layout is auto-corrected, the dropdown offers the corrected phrase as a clickable suggestion instead of staying silent.
  • **Loading indicator and screen-reader announcements in the dropdown.** A spinner shows while results are being fetched, and the number of results (or "nothing found") is announced to assistive technology.
  • **Phrase proximity (opt-in).** Among equally relevant matches, prefers a title that contains the query words as a phrase or in order over one where they are scattered. Off by default — enable and compare on your catalog.

Changed

  • **Rebalanced default field weights.** A word matched only in a long description, an attribute or a category now counts for less than before, so a full product whose specs merely mention a part no longer outranks the actual part on a mixed catalog (phones and spare parts). Title, SKU and brand weights are unchanged. Sites that customized field weights keep their own values.
  • **Broad searches paginate instead of stopping at 100.** The results page now keeps a larger ranked pool (up to a configurable ceiling on the Behavior tab) and pages through it with the theme's own pagination, so a common query no longer hides most of its matches. The extra depth is bounded so it stays fast on shared hosting.
  • **Category selector matches the search field.** The "All categories" dropdown next to the field now uses the same rounded shape, height and colours as the field, with its own chevron, instead of the browser's default control.
  • **Lighter bulk imports.** The search cache is now refreshed once per request instead of on every saved product, so importing or bulk-editing a large catalog no longer rewrites a cache marker on every item.
  • **Stricter searches no longer dead-end.** If an all-words match finds nothing, the search now falls back once to a looser any-word match before giving up, so a partial match still surfaces.
  • **More stable result order.** Equally relevant products now fall back to a deterministic order (sales, then rating), so the same query always returns the same ordering.
